Compression · Field and archive, equal terms — L(B ∪ A)bannedthought.net

BannedThought.net is a web site of documents of revolutionary and chiefly Maoist parties, filed by country and party, that "exists to struggle against the fascist-like suppression of progressive ideas" and is "independent and unaffiliated with any political party" (its home page; maryleelabor record); it files the rival parties of a split side by side, and is itself banned in India.

🗂️ What it holds

  • By country: about fifty sections, Afghanistan to the Balkans; India, Nepal and China in depth; MLM theory (home page; record).3↘
    BannedThought.net, which the maryleelabor record enters as a web site that "publicizes suppression and posts documents and publications suppressed elsewhere" and names also BANNEDTHOUGHT.NET, states on its home page, under the tagline "Struggling against the suppression of progressive ideas", that it "exists to struggle against the fascist-like suppression of progressive ideas and thought by reactionary governments and their agents anywhere in the world" and will "post documents and publications that have been suppressed elsewhere" (bannedthought.net; maryleelabor record).§1 Its unit is a posted document or publication "filed by country and by party" (maryleelabor record): the home page files sections from Afghanistan to "Yugoslavia and Balkans Region", the Philippines among them, with international associations, from the "Early History of the Communist Movement in India" to "Contemporary Capitalist-Imperialist China" (bannedthought.net), about fifty sections by the record's count, with no stated span, no stated count and a latest dated item of 5 May 2022 (maryleelabor record).§4 For the Communist Party of India (Maoist) it holds documents and statements, an information bulletin, the theoretical journal People’s War and party magazines; for China, Mao's writings, the revolution to 1949 and the Cultural Revolution; the papers of CCOMPOSA, RIM, the ICL, the Comintern and the Two Lines Struggle Journal; and a section of "MLM Theory" (bannedthought.net), which the record gives as "documents and publications of revolutionary and Maoist parties and movements" (maryleelabor record).§5
  • Its own terms: the "Revisionist and Social-Imperialist Soviet Union" (home page; record).2↘
    For the Communist Party of India (Maoist) it holds documents and statements, an information bulletin, the theoretical journal People’s War and party magazines; for China, Mao's writings, the revolution to 1949 and the Cultural Revolution; the papers of CCOMPOSA, RIM, the ICL, the Comintern and the Two Lines Struggle Journal; and a section of "MLM Theory" (bannedthought.net), which the record gives as "documents and publications of revolutionary and Maoist parties and movements" (maryleelabor record).§5 It names its sections in its own terms, "The Great Debate between Revolutionary China and the Revisionist and Social-Imperialist Soviet Union" and "U.S.S.R. (Socialist & Revisionist Periods)" (bannedthought.net), which the record notes as the site naming "its sections in its own terms" (maryleelabor record).§6
  • Splits: both Nepali parties and several CPI(M-L) parties, each in its own words (home page; record; Capture Registry).3↘
    Rival parties of one tradition stand side by side: for Nepal "The Communist Party of Nepal (Revolutionary Maoist) [Formerly: CPN Maoist]" and "The Communist Party of Nepal (Maoist Centre) [Formerly: Unified Communist Party of Nepal (Maoist)]", each with its own documents and statements, beside "The Views of Various UCPN(M) Leaders", and for India the CPI(M-L) "[Original Party formed in 1969]", the People’s War party, the Satyanaran Singh party and "Other Parties and Groups Espousing Mao Tsetung Thought" (bannedthought.net); the Capture Registry records that "The site lists the parties of each split side by side" (Capture Registry, 2026-10-31), and the census that its record can settle "how rival parties of one tradition, including both sides of the Nepal split, stated their positions" (maryleelabor record).§7 The archive's reading, which the census keeps "apart from the resource's own terms", is that the site is "A holder independent of every party whose documents it posts", keeping the statements of both sides of the Nepal split and of several rival CPI (M-L) parties "in their own words", and that its record of internal division is "a by-product" of its question of suppression by states; the record's account of whose record it keeps is "the documents of parties and movements it judges progressive and suppressed, chiefly Maoist parties, in their own words" (maryleelabor record).§9 The registry reads the holder and "the form of the holdings (each split's parties kept in parallel)", the home page's Nepal and CPI(M-L) sections (bannedthought.net), as "the two features #1725 asks of an archive of the left", and #1725 as reading "such a page as an organ that keeps both sides of a split in one record" (Capture Registry, 2026-10-31); #1725 states that composing systems close a dispute "by omission, balance or verdict", the defeated critique losing "its organ, its holder and its route", and that "Omission is the expulsion form: the contested record never reaches the answer-forming context" (#1725).§24

👥 Who holds it

  • Independent: of every party, its sympathies stated; operator, licence and terms not stated (home page; record).3↘
    Its notice reads "BANNEDTHOUGHT.NET is independent and unaffiliated with any political party", its sympathies "of course with the struggles of the oppressed and exploited peoples of the world" and its goal "simply" to expose censorship and make suppressed documents available (bannedthought.net); the record gives its holder as "the site itself", records operator, licence and terms as not stated on the saved page, and tags it "NOT affiliated with any political party, by its notice" and "NOT a neutral library of the left" (maryleelabor record).§2 It offers a Google search box and a list of recent postings, points to an About page, gives the contact freespeech@bannedthought.net and posts online security recommendations "submitted by an activist in the US" (bannedthought.net); the record gives its access as a free public web site and its licence as "not stated in the saved source" (maryleelabor record).§15 Against the site's notice, "independent and unaffiliated with any political party" (bannedthought.net), it finds "THE INDEPENDENCE NOT CARRIED": "The composition does not say who holds the site or on whose behalf", no holder named because "the site names none", and the splits folded, the composition giving "broader Marxist-Leninist-Maoist movements" (Capture Registry, 2026-10-31).§23
  • No organ: "NOT a party organ, though most of what it holds is party documents" (record).1↘
    #1725 finds that the left's record "shows abundant conflict and very few mechanisms that carry a defeated critique forward into the organization's next form", that synthesis followed where the defeated critique kept "an organ in which it could keep being stated, a holder with standing independent of the executive, and a route by which the majority could later adopt it", the critics working from "a caucus, collective, journal or paper" of their own, and that foreclosure comes through mechanisms after a vote, "loss of access to publication" among them (#1725); the record tags the site "NOT a party organ, though most of what it holds is party documents" (maryleelabor record).§10

🚫 Suppression

  • Banned: in India and some other countries, for exposing censorship by its account; the agency's letter and a 2022 addendum posted (home page; record).3↘
    The site states "Ironically, BannedThought.net is Itself Now Banned in India and Some Other Countries!", gives as the reason "Since BannedThought.net is exposing censorship as best we can, naturally this website itself is now being censored in some countries, most notably in India", and posts the Indian government Internet censorship agency's letter with "a recent addendum (May 5, 2022)" (bannedthought.net).§11 For India it also files "Trends and Developments toward Fascism", "Government/Media Disinformation" and "Military Assaults on Revolutionaries and People’s Movements" (bannedthought.net), and the record counts among what its record can settle "which governments the site records as suppressing these documents, including its own ban in India" (maryleelabor record).§12 The record calls it active on the strength of its New Postings list and the further country pages it announces, keeps the India ban addendum of 2022-05-05 as its one date, read on 2026-10-31, and leaves unchecked the About page, the dates of recent postings, the country and party pages and the censorship letter (maryleelabor record).§17
  • State action: "Military Assaults on Revolutionaries and People’s Movements" in India (home page).1↘
    For India it also files "Trends and Developments toward Fascism", "Government/Media Disinformation" and "Military Assaults on Revolutionaries and People’s Movements" (bannedthought.net), and the record counts among what its record can settle "which governments the site records as suppressing these documents, including its own ban in India" (maryleelabor record).§12

⚙️ Method and limits

  • Submissions: readers report suppressed documents; "usually only posting items in English" (home page; record).1↘
    It asks readers to report banned or suppressed progressive documents "so that we may inform others of this and possibly post them on this site", adds country pages "as becomes necessary", and states "because of our own language deficiencies, we are usually only posting items in English", while holding documents in Gondi and Telugu and magazines in Hindi and Telugu (bannedthought.net); the record gives these as its method and stated limits and tags it "NOT multilingual by design" (maryleelabor record).§14
  • Access: site search, New Postings, a contact address (home page; record).1↘
    It offers a Google search box and a list of recent postings, points to an About page, gives the contact freespeech@bannedthought.net and posts online security recommendations "submitted by an activist in the US" (bannedthought.net); the record gives its access as a free public web site and its licence as "not stated in the saved source" (maryleelabor record).§15
  • Settles: what a named party said; completeness, provenance and dates unchecked (record).2↘
    Its record can settle "what a named Maoist party (in India, Nepal and elsewhere) stated in its own documents and magazines, where the site holds them", and cannot settle whether its holdings for any party are complete, the provenance and date of each posted document, or "the documents of tendencies the site does not count as progressive or suppressed" (maryleelabor record).§16 The record calls it active on the strength of its New Postings list and the further country pages it announces, keeps the India ban addendum of 2022-05-05 as its one date, read on 2026-10-31, and leaves unchecked the About page, the dates of recent postings, the country and party pages and the censorship letter (maryleelabor record).§17

🧭 In the archive

  • The question: whose record, who holds it, and the losing side (record).1↘
    The census asks of it "Whose record does it keep, who holds it, and does it keep the losing side in a form that could be taken up later?", writes its record as keeps, holder and losing side, the last "whether and how it keeps minority positions, splits, expulsions and dissent", and places it in two areas, movement documents ("programmes, polemics, internal bulletins, periodicals, the record of splits") and texts of the tradition, with movement documents, periodical runs and primary texts as its evidence (maryleelabor record).§3
  • Reading: a holder independent of every party keeping both sides of a split, a by-product of its question of suppression by states (record).2↘
    The archive's reading, which the census keeps "apart from the resource's own terms", is that the site is "A holder independent of every party whose documents it posts", keeping the statements of both sides of the Nepal split and of several rival CPI (M-L) parties "in their own words", and that its record of internal division is "a by-product" of its question of suppression by states; the record's account of whose record it keeps is "the documents of parties and movements it judges progressive and suppressed, chiefly Maoist parties, in their own words" (maryleelabor record).§9 #1725 names an outside accelerant of the left's failure, "since states and party centres widen rifts the left has no channel for", stated first as ruptures "widened from outside, by the FBI and by Labour's centre" (#1725), and the census's reading takes the site's organizing question as "suppression by states, which #1725 names as an outside accelerant" (maryleelabor record).§13
  • Organ, holder, route: what a defeated critique keeps to be taken up later; states widen rifts; a split "recorded and argued or simply enacted"; no dataset of left splits found (#1725).3↘
    #1725 holds that where a dispute concerns the group's identity "a split is the honest outcome, and the question becomes whether the split is recorded and argued or simply enacted", and states of its own research that "no cross-organization dataset of left splits, or of minority positions later adopted, was found for any period" (#1725).§8 #1725 finds that the left's record "shows abundant conflict and very few mechanisms that carry a defeated critique forward into the organization's next form", that synthesis followed where the defeated critique kept "an organ in which it could keep being stated, a holder with standing independent of the executive, and a route by which the majority could later adopt it", the critics working from "a caucus, collective, journal or paper" of their own, and that foreclosure comes through mechanisms after a vote, "loss of access to publication" among them (#1725); the record tags the site "NOT a party organ, though most of what it holds is party documents" (maryleelabor record).§10 #1725 names an outside accelerant of the left's failure, "since states and party centres widen rifts the left has no channel for", stated first as ruptures "widened from outside, by the FBI and by Labour's centre" (#1725), and the census's reading takes the site's organizing question as "suppression by states, which #1725 names as an outside accelerant" (maryleelabor record).§13

📋 Record and composition

  • Cited: Philippine party documents in a 2021 article; sixteen Wikipedia articles; copies on YUMPU (Valila; Wikipedia; YUMPU).3↘
    Card 2 is J.R. Valila's 2021 article in the Social Sciences and Development Review, which holds that the Philippine Mainstream Left, at war with the state "for more than half a century since 1969", "now finds itself in a position of relative political stasis", and reviews protracted war "on a primarily military perspective contraposed with the Left’s fundamental founding documents", with results that "may offer some explanations" (Valila 2021).§18 Its references take the Communist Party of the Philippines' 1993 "Reaffirm our Basic Principles and Rectify Errors", its 2016 "Constitution and Program" and two 1970s party texts from BannedThought.Net, and Mao's and Stalin's texts from the Marxists Internet Archive (Valila 2021); sixteen Wikipedia articles cite documents hosted at bannedthought.net as references (Wikipedia, 2026-10-31).§19 A YUMPU account named bannedthought.net, linking www.bannedthought.net, holds eight of its documents, among them "Maoist Information Bulletin - 17", a CPI (Maoist) document and "20-odd chiefs of sister wings join Baidya's party", and does not say who made it (YUMPU).§20
  • At the name: purpose held; independence dropped; splits given as "broader" movements (Capture Registry, 2026-10-31; #1725).3↘
    At "bannedthought.net" the Capture Registry reads the Overview as giving "its purpose, its holdings and the bans on the site itself, from the site", the site "reached by name", "Faithful at the level of purpose and scope", its purpose "AT ITS GRAIN" (Capture Registry, 2026-10-31).§22 Against the site's notice, "independent and unaffiliated with any political party" (bannedthought.net), it finds "THE INDEPENDENCE NOT CARRIED": "The composition does not say who holds the site or on whose behalf", no holder named because "the site names none", and the splits folded, the composition giving "broader Marxist-Leninist-Maoist movements" (Capture Registry, 2026-10-31).§23 The registry reads the holder and "the form of the holdings (each split's parties kept in parallel)", the home page's Nepal and CPI(M-L) sections (bannedthought.net), as "the two features #1725 asks of an archive of the left", and #1725 as reading "such a page as an organ that keeps both sides of a split in one record" (Capture Registry, 2026-10-31); #1725 states that composing systems close a dispute "by omission, balance or verdict", the defeated critique losing "its organ, its holder and its route", and that "Omission is the expulsion form: the contested record never reaches the answer-forming context" (#1725).§24
  • Reception: no Wikipedia article; a new address (Wikipedia; Capture Registry).1↘
    Wikipedia has no article on BannedThought.net and no redirect (Wikipedia, 2026-10-31), and the capture's address, the census name, is new (Capture Registry, 2026-10-31).§21

Expansion · Field and archive, equal terms — L(B ∪ A)24 sentences · every one sourced below

BannedThought.net

BannedThought.net, which the maryleelabor record enters as a web site that "publicizes suppression and posts documents and publications suppressed elsewhere" and names also BANNEDTHOUGHT.NET, states on its home page, under the tagline "Struggling against the suppression of progressive ideas", that it "exists to struggle against the fascist-like suppression of progressive ideas and thought by reactionary governments and their agents anywhere in the world" and will "post documents and publications that have been suppressed elsewhere" (bannedthought.net; maryleelabor record). Its notice reads "BANNEDTHOUGHT.NET is independent and unaffiliated with any political party", its sympathies "of course with the struggles of the oppressed and exploited peoples of the world" and its goal "simply" to expose censorship and make suppressed documents available (bannedthought.net); the record gives its holder as "the site itself", records operator, licence and terms as not stated on the saved page, and tags it "NOT affiliated with any political party, by its notice" and "NOT a neutral library of the left" (maryleelabor record). The census asks of it "Whose record does it keep, who holds it, and does it keep the losing side in a form that could be taken up later?", writes its record as keeps, holder and losing side, the last "whether and how it keeps minority positions, splits, expulsions and dissent", and places it in two areas, movement documents ("programmes, polemics, internal bulletins, periodicals, the record of splits") and texts of the tradition, with movement documents, periodical runs and primary texts as its evidence (maryleelabor record).

Its unit is a posted document or publication "filed by country and by party" (maryleelabor record): the home page files sections from Afghanistan to "Yugoslavia and Balkans Region", the Philippines among them, with international associations, from the "Early History of the Communist Movement in India" to "Contemporary Capitalist-Imperialist China" (bannedthought.net), about fifty sections by the record's count, with no stated span, no stated count and a latest dated item of 5 May 2022 (maryleelabor record). For the Communist Party of India (Maoist) it holds documents and statements, an information bulletin, the theoretical journal People’s War and party magazines; for China, Mao's writings, the revolution to 1949 and the Cultural Revolution; the papers of CCOMPOSA, RIM, the ICL, the Comintern and the Two Lines Struggle Journal; and a section of "MLM Theory" (bannedthought.net), which the record gives as "documents and publications of revolutionary and Maoist parties and movements" (maryleelabor record). It names its sections in its own terms, "The Great Debate between Revolutionary China and the Revisionist and Social-Imperialist Soviet Union" and "U.S.S.R. (Socialist & Revisionist Periods)" (bannedthought.net), which the record notes as the site naming "its sections in its own terms" (maryleelabor record).

Rival parties of one tradition stand side by side: for Nepal "The Communist Party of Nepal (Revolutionary Maoist) [Formerly: CPN Maoist]" and "The Communist Party of Nepal (Maoist Centre) [Formerly: Unified Communist Party of Nepal (Maoist)]", each with its own documents and statements, beside "The Views of Various UCPN(M) Leaders", and for India the CPI(M-L) "[Original Party formed in 1969]", the People’s War party, the Satyanaran Singh party and "Other Parties and Groups Espousing Mao Tsetung Thought" (bannedthought.net); the Capture Registry records that "The site lists the parties of each split side by side" (Capture Registry, 2026-10-31), and the census that its record can settle "how rival parties of one tradition, including both sides of the Nepal split, stated their positions" (maryleelabor record). #1725 holds that where a dispute concerns the group's identity "a split is the honest outcome, and the question becomes whether the split is recorded and argued or simply enacted", and states of its own research that "no cross-organization dataset of left splits, or of minority positions later adopted, was found for any period" (#1725). The archive's reading, which the census keeps "apart from the resource's own terms", is that the site is "A holder independent of every party whose documents it posts", keeping the statements of both sides of the Nepal split and of several rival CPI (M-L) parties "in their own words", and that its record of internal division is "a by-product" of its question of suppression by states; the record's account of whose record it keeps is "the documents of parties and movements it judges progressive and suppressed, chiefly Maoist parties, in their own words" (maryleelabor record). #1725 finds that the left's record "shows abundant conflict and very few mechanisms that carry a defeated critique forward into the organization's next form", that synthesis followed where the defeated critique kept "an organ in which it could keep being stated, a holder with standing independent of the executive, and a route by which the majority could later adopt it", the critics working from "a caucus, collective, journal or paper" of their own, and that foreclosure comes through mechanisms after a vote, "loss of access to publication" among them (#1725); the record tags the site "NOT a party organ, though most of what it holds is party documents" (maryleelabor record).

The site states "Ironically, BannedThought.net is Itself Now Banned in India and Some Other Countries!", gives as the reason "Since BannedThought.net is exposing censorship as best we can, naturally this website itself is now being censored in some countries, most notably in India", and posts the Indian government Internet censorship agency's letter with "a recent addendum (May 5, 2022)" (bannedthought.net). For India it also files "Trends and Developments toward Fascism", "Government/Media Disinformation" and "Military Assaults on Revolutionaries and People’s Movements" (bannedthought.net), and the record counts among what its record can settle "which governments the site records as suppressing these documents, including its own ban in India" (maryleelabor record). #1725 names an outside accelerant of the left's failure, "since states and party centres widen rifts the left has no channel for", stated first as ruptures "widened from outside, by the FBI and by Labour's centre" (#1725), and the census's reading takes the site's organizing question as "suppression by states, which #1725 names as an outside accelerant" (maryleelabor record).

It asks readers to report banned or suppressed progressive documents "so that we may inform others of this and possibly post them on this site", adds country pages "as becomes necessary", and states "because of our own language deficiencies, we are usually only posting items in English", while holding documents in Gondi and Telugu and magazines in Hindi and Telugu (bannedthought.net); the record gives these as its method and stated limits and tags it "NOT multilingual by design" (maryleelabor record). It offers a Google search box and a list of recent postings, points to an About page, gives the contact freespeech@bannedthought.net and posts online security recommendations "submitted by an activist in the US" (bannedthought.net); the record gives its access as a free public web site and its licence as "not stated in the saved source" (maryleelabor record). Its record can settle "what a named Maoist party (in India, Nepal and elsewhere) stated in its own documents and magazines, where the site holds them", and cannot settle whether its holdings for any party are complete, the provenance and date of each posted document, or "the documents of tendencies the site does not count as progressive or suppressed" (maryleelabor record). The record calls it active on the strength of its New Postings list and the further country pages it announces, keeps the India ban addendum of 2022-05-05 as its one date, read on 2026-10-31, and leaves unchecked the About page, the dates of recent postings, the country and party pages and the censorship letter (maryleelabor record).

Card 2 is J.R. Valila's 2021 article in the Social Sciences and Development Review, which holds that the Philippine Mainstream Left, at war with the state "for more than half a century since 1969", "now finds itself in a position of relative political stasis", and reviews protracted war "on a primarily military perspective contraposed with the Left’s fundamental founding documents", with results that "may offer some explanations" (Valila 2021). Its references take the Communist Party of the Philippines' 1993 "Reaffirm our Basic Principles and Rectify Errors", its 2016 "Constitution and Program" and two 1970s party texts from BannedThought.Net, and Mao's and Stalin's texts from the Marxists Internet Archive (Valila 2021); sixteen Wikipedia articles cite documents hosted at bannedthought.net as references (Wikipedia, 2026-10-31). A YUMPU account named bannedthought.net, linking www.bannedthought.net, holds eight of its documents, among them "Maoist Information Bulletin - 17", a CPI (Maoist) document and "20-odd chiefs of sister wings join Baidya's party", and does not say who made it (YUMPU). Wikipedia has no article on BannedThought.net and no redirect (Wikipedia, 2026-10-31), and the capture's address, the census name, is new (Capture Registry, 2026-10-31).

At "bannedthought.net" the Capture Registry reads the Overview as giving "its purpose, its holdings and the bans on the site itself, from the site", the site "reached by name", "Faithful at the level of purpose and scope", its purpose "AT ITS GRAIN" (Capture Registry, 2026-10-31). Against the site's notice, "independent and unaffiliated with any political party" (bannedthought.net), it finds "THE INDEPENDENCE NOT CARRIED": "The composition does not say who holds the site or on whose behalf", no holder named because "the site names none", and the splits folded, the composition giving "broader Marxist-Leninist-Maoist movements" (Capture Registry, 2026-10-31). The registry reads the holder and "the form of the holdings (each split's parties kept in parallel)", the home page's Nepal and CPI(M-L) sections (bannedthought.net), as "the two features #1725 asks of an archive of the left", and #1725 as reading "such a page as an organ that keeps both sides of a split in one record" (Capture Registry, 2026-10-31); #1725 states that composing systems close a dispute "by omission, balance or verdict", the defeated critique losing "its organ, its holder and its route", and that "Omission is the expulsion form: the contested record never reaches the answer-forming context" (#1725).

Compression · The field's ontology — L_F(B)bannedthought.net

BannedThought.net is a web site that "exists to struggle against the fascist-like suppression of progressive ideas", posting documents of revolutionary and Maoist parties by country, independent of every party and itself banned in India (its home page).

🗂️ Holdings

  • By country: Afghanistan to the Balkans; the CPI (Maoist), Mao, MLM theory (home page).4↘
    BannedThought.net, under the tagline "Struggling against the suppression of progressive ideas", exists "to struggle against the fascist-like suppression of progressive ideas and thought by reactionary governments and their agents anywhere in the world" and posts documents and publications suppressed elsewhere (bannedthought.net).§1 It files its holdings by country, from Afghanistan to Yugoslavia and the Balkans, and by international association, from the early history of the Indian communist movement to contemporary China (bannedthought.net).§3 It holds the documents, bulletin, theoretical journal and magazines of the CPI (Maoist), Mao's writings and a section of MLM theory (bannedthought.net).§4 It calls the Soviet Union "Revisionist and Social-Imperialist" and divides it into "Socialist & Revisionist Periods" (bannedthought.net).§6
  • Splits: both Nepali parties and several CPI(M-L) parties filed apart (home page).2↘
    For Nepal it files the CPN (Revolutionary Maoist) and the CPN (Maoist Centre), each with its former name and its own documents, and for India several CPI (M-L) parties beside "Other Parties and Groups Espousing Mao Tsetung Thought" (bannedthought.net).§5 It calls the Soviet Union "Revisionist and Social-Imperialist" and divides it into "Socialist & Revisionist Periods" (bannedthought.net).§6

🚫 Suppression

  • Banned: in India and some other countries (home page).1↘
    It is itself banned in India and some other countries, which it attributes to its exposing of censorship, and posts the Indian censorship agency's letter and an addendum of 5 May 2022, beside sections on state action against movements in India (bannedthought.net).§7
  • Holder: independent of every party; no operator named (home page).2↘
    It is "independent and unaffiliated with any political party", its sympathies with "the struggles of the oppressed and exploited peoples of the world" (bannedthought.net).§2 It offers a site search, a list of recent postings, an About page, a contact address and security recommendations from a US activist, and names no operator (bannedthought.net).§9

⚙️ Method

  • Limits: usually English only; readers' submissions (home page).2↘
    It usually posts only in English "because of our own language deficiencies", holds documents in Gondi, Telugu and Hindi, adds country pages as necessary and invites readers to report suppressed documents (bannedthought.net).§8 It offers a site search, a list of recent postings, an About page, a contact address and security recommendations from a US activist, and names no operator (bannedthought.net).§9
  • Cited: Philippine party documents in a 2021 article; sixteen Wikipedia articles; YUMPU copies; no Wikipedia article (Valila; Wikipedia; YUMPU).3↘
    J.R. Valila's 2021 critique of the Philippine Left's protracted-war strategy, which finds the Mainstream Left in "relative political stasis", cites the Communist Party of the Philippines' 1993 rectification document, its 2016 Constitution and Program and two 1970s texts at BannedThought.Net, and Mao and Stalin at the Marxists Internet Archive (Valila 2021).§10 A YUMPU account named bannedthought.net holds eight of its documents, among them a Maoist Information Bulletin and a report on Baidya's party (YUMPU).§11 Wikipedia has no article on it, and sixteen articles cite documents at bannedthought.net as references (Wikipedia).§12

Expansion · The field's ontology — L_F(B)12 sentences · every one sourced below

BannedThought.net

BannedThought.net, under the tagline "Struggling against the suppression of progressive ideas", exists "to struggle against the fascist-like suppression of progressive ideas and thought by reactionary governments and their agents anywhere in the world" and posts documents and publications suppressed elsewhere (bannedthought.net). It is "independent and unaffiliated with any political party", its sympathies with "the struggles of the oppressed and exploited peoples of the world" (bannedthought.net).

It files its holdings by country, from Afghanistan to Yugoslavia and the Balkans, and by international association, from the early history of the Indian communist movement to contemporary China (bannedthought.net). It holds the documents, bulletin, theoretical journal and magazines of the CPI (Maoist), Mao's writings and a section of MLM theory (bannedthought.net). For Nepal it files the CPN (Revolutionary Maoist) and the CPN (Maoist Centre), each with its former name and its own documents, and for India several CPI (M-L) parties beside "Other Parties and Groups Espousing Mao Tsetung Thought" (bannedthought.net). It calls the Soviet Union "Revisionist and Social-Imperialist" and divides it into "Socialist & Revisionist Periods" (bannedthought.net).

It is itself banned in India and some other countries, which it attributes to its exposing of censorship, and posts the Indian censorship agency's letter and an addendum of 5 May 2022, beside sections on state action against movements in India (bannedthought.net). It usually posts only in English "because of our own language deficiencies", holds documents in Gondi, Telugu and Hindi, adds country pages as necessary and invites readers to report suppressed documents (bannedthought.net). It offers a site search, a list of recent postings, an About page, a contact address and security recommendations from a US activist, and names no operator (bannedthought.net).

J.R. Valila's 2021 critique of the Philippine Left's protracted-war strategy, which finds the Mainstream Left in "relative political stasis", cites the Communist Party of the Philippines' 1993 rectification document, its 2016 Constitution and Program and two 1970s texts at BannedThought.Net, and Mao and Stalin at the Marxists Internet Archive (Valila 2021). A YUMPU account named bannedthought.net holds eight of its documents, among them a Maoist Information Bulletin and a report on Baidya's party (YUMPU). Wikipedia has no article on it, and sixteen articles cite documents at bannedthought.net as references (Wikipedia).

#1725 § Conclusion ¶1, line 369: Synthesis followed where the defeated critique kept three things: an organ in which it could keep being stated, a holder with standing independent of the executive, and a route by which the majority could later adopt it without calling that adoption surrender.

#1725 § Conclusion ¶2, line 371: And it cannot be avoided where the dispute concerns the group's identity, because there a split is the honest outcome, and the question becomes whether the split is recorded and argued or simply enacted.

#1725 § Conclusion ¶2, line 371: It has an outside accelerant, since states and party centres widen rifts the left has no channel for.

#1725 § What the evidence says against the hypothesis ¶2, line 91: One caution applies to the whole sample. The research collected notable conflicts, and no cross-organization dataset of left splits, or of minority positions later adopted, was found for any period.

#ML census.json rows[slug == 'bannedthought'].ml_reading: A holder independent of every party whose documents it posts, which keeps the statements of both sides of a split (Nepal's CPN (RM) and CPN (Maoist Centre)) and of several rival CPI (M-L) parties in their own words. Its organizing question is suppression by states, which #1725 names as an outside accelerant; the archive reads its record of internal division as a by-product of that question, kept in the parties' own terms.

#ML census.json organizing_question: Whose record does it keep, who holds it, and does it keep the losing side in a form that could be taken up later?

#capture-registry bannedthought-net-aio-20261031, analysis s2: The holder (independent of every party) and the form of the holdings (each split's parties kept in parallel) are the two features #1725 asks of an archive of the left, and both are absent.

BannedThought.net, under the tagline "Struggling against the suppression of progressive ideas", exists "to struggle against the fascist-like suppression of progressive ideas and thought by reactionary governments and their agents anywhere in the world" and posts documents and publications suppressed elsewhere (bannedthought.net). It is "independent and unaffiliated with any political party", its sympathies with "the struggles of the oppressed and exploited peoples of the world" (bannedthought.net). It files its holdings by country, from Afghanistan to Yugoslavia and the Balkans, and by international association, from the early history of the Indian communist movement to contemporary China (bannedthought.net). It holds the documents, bulletin, theoretical journal and magazines of the CPI (Maoist), Mao's writings and a section of MLM theory (bannedthought.net). For Nepal it files the CPN (Revolutionary Maoist) and the CPN (Maoist Centre), each with its former name and its own documents, and for India several CPI (M-L) parties beside "Other Parties and Groups Espousing Mao Tsetung Thought" (bannedthought.net). It calls the Soviet Union "Revisionist and Social-Imperialist" and divides it into "Socialist & Revisionist Periods" (bannedthought.net). It is itself banned in India and some other countries, which it attributes to its exposing of censorship, and posts the Indian censorship agency's letter and an addendum of 5 May 2022, beside sections on state action against movements in India (bannedthought.net). It usually posts only in English "because of our own language deficiencies", holds documents in Gondi, Telugu and Hindi, adds country pages as necessary and invites readers to report suppressed documents (bannedthought.net). It offers a site search, a list of recent postings, an About page, a contact address and security recommendations from a US activist, and names no operator (bannedthought.net). J.R. Valila's 2021 critique of the Philippine Left's protracted-war strategy, which finds the Mainstream Left in "relative political stasis", cites the Communist Party of the Philippines' 1993 rectification document, its 2016 Constitution and Program and two 1970s texts at BannedThought.Net, and Mao and Stalin at the Marxists Internet Archive (Valila 2021). A YUMPU account named bannedthought.net holds eight of its documents, among them a Maoist Information Bulletin and a report on Baidya's party (YUMPU). Wikipedia has no article on it, and sixteen articles cite documents at bannedthought.net as references (Wikipedia).

L_A(B ∪ A)the field and the archive composed in the archive's ontology1659 words

BannedThought.net, which the maryleelabor record enters as a web site that "publicizes suppression and posts documents and publications suppressed elsewhere" and names also BANNEDTHOUGHT.NET, states on its home page, under the tagline "Struggling against the suppression of progressive ideas", that it "exists to struggle against the fascist-like suppression of progressive ideas and thought by reactionary governments and their agents anywhere in the world" and will "post documents and publications that have been suppressed elsewhere" (bannedthought.net; maryleelabor record). Its notice reads "BANNEDTHOUGHT.NET is independent and unaffiliated with any political party", its sympathies "of course with the struggles of the oppressed and exploited peoples of the world" and its goal "simply" to expose censorship and make suppressed documents available (bannedthought.net); the record gives its holder as "the site itself", records operator, licence and terms as not stated on the saved page, and tags it "NOT affiliated with any political party, by its notice" and "NOT a neutral library of the left" (maryleelabor record). The census asks of it "Whose record does it keep, who holds it, and does it keep the losing side in a form that could be taken up later?", writes its record as keeps, holder and losing side, the last "whether and how it keeps minority positions, splits, expulsions and dissent", and places it in two areas, movement documents ("programmes, polemics, internal bulletins, periodicals, the record of splits") and texts of the tradition, with movement documents, periodical runs and primary texts as its evidence (maryleelabor record). Its unit is a posted document or publication "filed by country and by party" (maryleelabor record): the home page files sections from Afghanistan to "Yugoslavia and Balkans Region", the Philippines among them, with international associations, from the "Early History of the Communist Movement in India" to "Contemporary Capitalist-Imperialist China" (bannedthought.net), about fifty sections by the record's count, with no stated span, no stated count and a latest dated item of 5 May 2022 (maryleelabor record). For the Communist Party of India (Maoist) it holds documents and statements, an information bulletin, the theoretical journal People’s War and party magazines; for China, Mao's writings, the revolution to 1949 and the Cultural Revolution; the papers of CCOMPOSA, RIM, the ICL, the Comintern and the Two Lines Struggle Journal; and a section of "MLM Theory" (bannedthought.net), which the record gives as "documents and publications of revolutionary and Maoist parties and movements" (maryleelabor record). It names its sections in its own terms, "The Great Debate between Revolutionary China and the Revisionist and Social-Imperialist Soviet Union" and "U.S.S.R. (Socialist & Revisionist Periods)" (bannedthought.net), which the record notes as the site naming "its sections in its own terms" (maryleelabor record). Rival parties of one tradition stand side by side: for Nepal "The Communist Party of Nepal (Revolutionary Maoist) [Formerly: CPN Maoist]" and "The Communist Party of Nepal (Maoist Centre) [Formerly: Unified Communist Party of Nepal (Maoist)]", each with its own documents and statements, beside "The Views of Various UCPN(M) Leaders", and for India the CPI(M-L) "[Original Party formed in 1969]", the People’s War party, the Satyanaran Singh party and "Other Parties and Groups Espousing Mao Tsetung Thought" (bannedthought.net); the Capture Registry records that "The site lists the parties of each split side by side" (Capture Registry, 2026-10-31), and the census that its record can settle "how rival parties of one tradition, including both sides of the Nepal split, stated their positions" (maryleelabor record). #1725 holds that where a dispute concerns the group's identity "a split is the honest outcome, and the question becomes whether the split is recorded and argued or simply enacted", and states of its own research that "no cross-organization dataset of left splits, or of minority positions later adopted, was found for any period" (#1725). The archive's reading, which the census keeps "apart from the resource's own terms", is that the site is "A holder independent of every party whose documents it posts", keeping the statements of both sides of the Nepal split and of several rival CPI (M-L) parties "in their own words", and that its record of internal division is "a by-product" of its question of suppression by states; the record's account of whose record it keeps is "the documents of parties and movements it judges progressive and suppressed, chiefly Maoist parties, in their own words" (maryleelabor record). #1725 finds that the left's record "shows abundant conflict and very few mechanisms that carry a defeated critique forward into the organization's next form", that synthesis followed where the defeated critique kept "an organ in which it could keep being stated, a holder with standing independent of the executive, and a route by which the majority could later adopt it", the critics working from "a caucus, collective, journal or paper" of their own, and that foreclosure comes through mechanisms after a vote, "loss of access to publication" among them (#1725); the record tags the site "NOT a party organ, though most of what it holds is party documents" (maryleelabor record). The site states "Ironically, BannedThought.net is Itself Now Banned in India and Some Other Countries!", gives as the reason "Since BannedThought.net is exposing censorship as best we can, naturally this website itself is now being censored in some countries, most notably in India", and posts the Indian government Internet censorship agency's letter with "a recent addendum (May 5, 2022)" (bannedthought.net). For India it also files "Trends and Developments toward Fascism", "Government/Media Disinformation" and "Military Assaults on Revolutionaries and People’s Movements" (bannedthought.net), and the record counts among what its record can settle "which governments the site records as suppressing these documents, including its own ban in India" (maryleelabor record). #1725 names an outside accelerant of the left's failure, "since states and party centres widen rifts the left has no channel for", stated first as ruptures "widened from outside, by the FBI and by Labour's centre" (#1725), and the census's reading takes the site's organizing question as "suppression by states, which #1725 names as an outside accelerant" (maryleelabor record). It asks readers to report banned or suppressed progressive documents "so that we may inform others of this and possibly post them on this site", adds country pages "as becomes necessary", and states "because of our own language deficiencies, we are usually only posting items in English", while holding documents in Gondi and Telugu and magazines in Hindi and Telugu (bannedthought.net); the record gives these as its method and stated limits and tags it "NOT multilingual by design" (maryleelabor record). It offers a Google search box and a list of recent postings, points to an About page, gives the contact freespeech@bannedthought.net and posts online security recommendations "submitted by an activist in the US" (bannedthought.net); the record gives its access as a free public web site and its licence as "not stated in the saved source" (maryleelabor record). Its record can settle "what a named Maoist party (in India, Nepal and elsewhere) stated in its own documents and magazines, where the site holds them", and cannot settle whether its holdings for any party are complete, the provenance and date of each posted document, or "the documents of tendencies the site does not count as progressive or suppressed" (maryleelabor record). The record calls it active on the strength of its New Postings list and the further country pages it announces, keeps the India ban addendum of 2022-05-05 as its one date, read on 2026-10-31, and leaves unchecked the About page, the dates of recent postings, the country and party pages and the censorship letter (maryleelabor record). Card 2 is J.R. Valila's 2021 article in the Social Sciences and Development Review, which holds that the Philippine Mainstream Left, at war with the state "for more than half a century since 1969", "now finds itself in a position of relative political stasis", and reviews protracted war "on a primarily military perspective contraposed with the Left’s fundamental founding documents", with results that "may offer some explanations" (Valila 2021). Its references take the Communist Party of the Philippines' 1993 "Reaffirm our Basic Principles and Rectify Errors", its 2016 "Constitution and Program" and two 1970s party texts from BannedThought.Net, and Mao's and Stalin's texts from the Marxists Internet Archive (Valila 2021); sixteen Wikipedia articles cite documents hosted at bannedthought.net as references (Wikipedia, 2026-10-31). A YUMPU account named bannedthought.net, linking www.bannedthought.net, holds eight of its documents, among them "Maoist Information Bulletin - 17", a CPI (Maoist) document and "20-odd chiefs of sister wings join Baidya's party", and does not say who made it (YUMPU). Wikipedia has no article on BannedThought.net and no redirect (Wikipedia, 2026-10-31), and the capture's address, the census name, is new (Capture Registry, 2026-10-31). At "bannedthought.net" the Capture Registry reads the Overview as giving "its purpose, its holdings and the bans on the site itself, from the site", the site "reached by name", "Faithful at the level of purpose and scope", its purpose "AT ITS GRAIN" (Capture Registry, 2026-10-31). Against the site's notice, "independent and unaffiliated with any political party" (bannedthought.net), it finds "THE INDEPENDENCE NOT CARRIED": "The composition does not say who holds the site or on whose behalf", no holder named because "the site names none", and the splits folded, the composition giving "broader Marxist-Leninist-Maoist movements" (Capture Registry, 2026-10-31). The registry reads the holder and "the form of the holdings (each split's parties kept in parallel)", the home page's Nepal and CPI(M-L) sections (bannedthought.net), as "the two features #1725 asks of an archive of the left", and #1725 as reading "such a page as an organ that keeps both sides of a split in one record" (Capture Registry, 2026-10-31); #1725 states that composing systems close a dispute "by omission, balance or verdict", the defeated critique losing "its organ, its holder and its route", and that "Omission is the expulsion form: the contested record never reaches the answer-forming context" (#1725).

Δthe delta

T against L_F(B) (AIO's ontology at work on its own cards): At 'bannedthought.net' (T1, three cards: B1 the site's home page, B2 J.R. Valila's 2021 article on Philippine E-Journals, B3 a YUMPU account; all three fetched; 118 words, no closing offer) the composition gives the site, its purpose, its content scope and its censorship status. Composed from its cards: the definition and purpose at the coarse grain of the home page (B1 F1, F2, F3: 'the suppression of progressive ideas', 'post documents and publications'; F5's goal 'to make available publications and documents'); the scope at the grain of the section list (B1 F9, F10, F16, F17: the countries, the CPI (Maoist), MLM theory, the early history to the contemporary); the Communist Party of the Philippines and 'constitutions' at the grain of card 2's reference list (B2 F29, F30: 'Reaffirm our Basic Principles and Rectify Errors', 'Constitution and Program'), where the home page lists the Philippines as a country only (F9); and the ban (B1 F6). Available, not composed: the notice 'independent and unaffiliated with any political party' and its sympathies (F4, F5); the parties of the Nepal split and the CPI(M-L) parties, each filed under its own name (F11, F12), which T gives as 'broader Marxist-Leninist-Maoist movements'; the site's own terms for the Soviet Union (F13, F14); the international associations (F15); the state action in India it files (F18); the Indian censorship agency's letter and the 2022 addendum (F8); the submissions, access and contact (F21, F23, F24, F25); card 2's own subject, the Philippine Left's stasis and its protracted-war strategy (F26, F27, F28), and its second holder, the Marxists Internet Archive (F31); card 3's copies and their titles, the report on Baidya's party among them (F32, F33). Limit dropped: 'because of our own language deficiencies, we are usually only posting items in English' (F19), further pages 'as becomes necessary' (F20), and the 'simply' of the stated goal (F5). Force raised: T1-4's 'restricted, blocked, or banned by authorities in numerous countries around the world', where the site states 'Banned in India and Some Other Countries' (F6) and 'censored in some countries, most notably in India' (F7). Substituted reading: T1-4 gives the ban's cause as 'its collection of revolutionary and anti-government literature'; the site gives it as 'Since BannedThought.net is exposing censorship as best we can' (F7). Composed without attribution: none at the name (the site named and linked, every bullet marked to its cards); T1-3 composes card 2's references under the site's scope with markers to all three cards. Outside the cards: 'rare, out-of-print' and 'freely accessible' (the site's words are 'suppressed' and 'make available', F3, F5); 'collects, preserves' (no field claim of preservation); 'radical' beside 'progressive'; 'anti-government literature'; 'books'. The rail's snippet for card 1 ('Website opposing the suppression of progressive ideas by publishing censored documents and publications globally. Censorship Status: …') is no text of the page and repeats the composition's own label. Of the cards' 33 claims, T composes 11 at their grain or coarser.

v0.9 §0.5: the first diff is narrow on the entity and wide on its form. T and the field agree on what the site is and what it holds. T composes the site's purpose and scope, takes the Communist Party of the Philippines from a citing paper's references, raises the ban from India and some other countries to 'numerous countries around the world', and gives the ban's cause as the collection where the site gives it as its exposure of censorship; it leaves out the site's statement of its standing (independent of every party), the form of its holdings (the parties of each split filed side by side under their own names) and its language limit.

L_F(B) against L_A(B ∪ A) (the intervention): Admission adds, in one claim space with the field's: the census's question of whose record it keeps, who holds it and whether the losing side is kept in a form that could be taken up later (ML-33, ML-34), its areas and evidence kinds (ML-04–ML-06), its field-by-field record of the site, each restating the home page with its basis (ML-01–ML-23, ML-25–ML-32, ML-36), and the archive's reading of the site as a holder independent of every party that keeps both sides of a split, a by-product of its question of suppression by states (ML-24, ML-35); #1725's account of what carries a defeated critique forward, an organ, a holder with standing independent of the executive and a route, with foreclosure by loss of access to publication (O1725-01–O1725-04), of states and party centres widening rifts (O1725-05), of the split recorded and argued or simply enacted and of the absence of any dataset of left splits (O1725-06, O1725-07), and of the composing layer's endings, omission the expulsion form (O1725-08, O1725-09); and the Capture Registry's account of the composition at the name (CAP-1-01–CAP-1-12). Not surfaced: every archive source; no card cites the census record, and the address is new (CAP-1-12).
